findings.message: AZDO_REPO is derived with `${FLEET_REPO_URL##*/}` and no check of the result. A trailing slash gives an empty value, and a `.git` suffix gives `repo.git`. The empty value is exported silently, so pr-azdo later fails with no hint that the pod derived the name wrongly. Strip a trailing `/` and `.git` before taking the last path segment. If the result is empty, warn or fail instead of exporting an empty AZDO_REPO. Add variant cases for the trailing slash, the `.git` suffix and an empty FLEET_REPO_URL.
findings.scenario: FLEET_REPO_URL=https://dev.azure.com/o/p/_git/repo/ -> AZDO_REPO is empty and the agent's pr-azdo cannot open the PR. FLEET_REPO_URL=.../_git/repo.git -> AZDO_REPO=repo.git, the wrong repo name. The test only covers the plain `/r` URL and the preset values.

findings.message: The `≥` for `hosted_s` and `prs_open` was added to the band (view.ts:27), the pane (view.ts:69-70), the shell table (report-render.sh) and report.html. The new tests only check the JSON `totals.partial`. No test checks that any renderer prints the marker. The existing report.spec.ts and pane.test.tsx cases were not extended. Add table-driven render tests, with partial containing hosted_s, prs_open, or both, over the band, status, pane, the REPORT_TABLE output and the HTML tiles.
findings.scenario: Delete `ge(view.report, 'prs_open')` from bandText, or `ge("hosted_s")` from REPORT_TABLE. The build and PR 500 cases in ac35 and all view tests stay green, but the band shows `0 PRs open` with no `≥` after a PR read failure.

findings.message: The commit replaces `head -n1` / `head -1` with awk in six places: workspace.sh change_branch, doctor-azure.sh pipeline_var, feature-graph.sh doc_field, report.sh first_obj, workitem.sh work_item_id, and the settings.sh check. The test exercises only the settings check and whatever `feature plan` happens to reach. The other call sites have no variant test with a multi-line producer under pipefail, so reverting them leaves the suite green. Add one case per site, each with input that produces more than one matching line.
findings.scenario: Revert `awk 'NR == 1'` to `head -1` in work_item_id with a status.md holding several matching lines under `set -o pipefail`. A large producer gets SIGPIPE and exit 141 can surface, yet ac37 passes.

findings.message: `partial` infers which read failed by substring-matching the free-text `.note` (`test("build")`, `test("pr")`). This is a second, implicit copy of the note vocabulary produced in report-query.sh. Any note containing `pr` (for example 'improper' or 'process') would mark prs_open partial. A note that names a read differently would silently drop the marker. Also, wall_s is derived from `queued` and has no partial flag when the build read fails. Emit a structured unread list (for example `.unread: ["build"]`) from the query and match on it.
findings.scenario: A future note 'unread: processes' sets `prs_open` partial for a row whose PR read succeeded. A build 500 leaves `queued` null, so wall_s shows without `≥`.

findings.message: The failed and complete variants assert `.job == "fleet-003-b"`, the same name the row already carries from the records. That cannot tell the Job's own name from the fallback to `$r.job`. Make the stub Job's name differ from the record's job, and assert the Job's own name in those two variants.
findings.scenario: Break the `$j.job` branch so the row always uses `$r.job`. The failed and complete variants still pass because both names are fleet-003-b.
